clinician.final_diagnosis: subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord and polyneuropathy secondary to concomitant nitrous oxide abuse and autoimmune atrophic gastritis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A man in his 30s presented with subacute onset (3 weeks) of sensory ataxia characterized by patchy symmetric numbness and paresthesias below the umbilicus, positive Romberg sign, wide-based gait, absent lower extremity vibratory sense and proprioception, and absent reflexes, following 4-5 months of heavy nitrous oxide abuse (450 canisters daily). MRI of the spinal cord demonstrated patchy T2 hyperintensity in the dorsal columns extending from C3 to T9-T10 without enhancement (E003), pathognomonic for subacute combined degeneration. Laboratory evaluation revealed functional vitamin B12 deficiency despite normal serum B12 (672 pg/mL), evidenced by elevated methylmalonic acid (5.86 µmol/L) and homocysteine (32 µmol/L), with macrocytosis (MCV 94 fL) (E004). Intrinsic factor blocking antibodies were present (E004), confirming autoimmune gastritis. Gastric biopsy demonstrated chronic inflammation involving the oxyntic mucosa (body-fundic region) (E005), consistent with autoimmune gastritis affecting parietal cells, with negative testing for H. pylori, celiac disease, and giardia. The clinical picture was attributed to concomitant nitrous oxide-induced functional B12 inactivation superimposed on underlying autoimmune gastritis causing B12 malabsorption, in the setting of historically borderline B12 levels.
